name: What is the difference between a tankless and a traditional water heater?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a tankless and a traditional water heater?

acceptedAnswer.text: A traditional water heater stores and heats a large tank of water, providing a limited supply of hot water until the tank is depleted. Tankless water heaters, also known as on-demand water heaters, heat water directly as it flows through the unit, supplying a continuous flow of hot water without a storage tank. Tankless units are generally more energy-efficient and take up less space, while traditional units often have lower upfront costs. Your choice depends on your household's hot water needs and budget.
acceptedAnswer.description: Traditional heaters store hot water in a tank, offering a limited supply. Tankless units heat water on demand for continuous supply, are more efficient, but often cost more upfront.
